review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped for muVal and for every `simp only [muVal …]` use. The file has no @[simp] attributes. The only simp-interface problem I found is that `muVal` has no unfolding equations. Every use re-proves the same two facts ad hoc through `simp only [muVal, dite_eq_left …]` / `dite_eq_right`. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim that any simp call fails or loops. I did not check whether the 20 muVal hits in N1000000WeakDuality.lean refer to a different declaration. The other `simp_all` calls are terminal-goal closers, not interface issues. I did not recommend further simp attributes.

findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def muVal (q : ℕ) (hq3 : 3 ≤ q) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if hbad : 0 < badCountQ q n then
findings.problem: `muVal` is a dependent `if` whose `then` branch mentions the proof `hbad` (through `leastGoodAbove hq3 hbad`). The file provides no equation lemmas for it, neither for the bad case nor for the good case. Every user therefore restates the unfolded value and re-proves it with `simp only [muVal, dite_eq_left h]` or `dite_eq_right (by omega : ¬ 0 < …)`. This happens at lines 104, 111, 116, 170, 201, 251, 272, 323 and 326. Four of the nine proofs, at lines 104, 116, 272 and 323, restate the same full RHS for different `n`, `n'` and `hbad`. Line 170 states the same equation with `i`/`set` abbreviations, and line 326 re-proves it for `n` again. The three zero-case proofs, at lines 111, 201 and 251, each build a `¬ 0 < badCountQ …` side proof by `omega`. Because there is no canonical rewrite rule, a bare `simp` cannot reduce `muVal q hq3 n'` even when `badCountQ q n' = 0` is in context. The proofs therefore need these `have … := by simp only [muVal, …]` blocks and a late `simp_all` (lines 112 and 292). `simp_all` there depends on the `hmn'` hypotheses being in context.
findings.proposed_change:
Right after the definition, add two equation lemmas:
`theorem muVal_of_pos {q} (hq3 : 3 ≤ q) {n} (hbad : 0 < badCountQ q n) : muVal q hq3 n = leastGoodAbove hq3 hbad * q + ((q - 1) / 2 - n / q ^ (leastGoodAbove hq3 hbad) % q) := dif_pos hbad`
and
`@[simp] theorem muVal_of_eq_zero {q} (hq3 : 3 ≤ q) {n} (h : badCountQ q n = 0) : muVal q hq3 n = 0 := dif_neg (by omega)`.
Only the zero case should be `@[simp]`. Its side condition `badCountQ q n = 0` can be discharged from hypotheses, and its RHS is a normal form with no unfolding. The `pos` lemma should stay unannotated and be used with `rw [muVal_of_pos hq3 hbad]`, because its RHS reintroduces a proof-dependent term. Then replace the nine local `have … := by simp only [muVal, …]` blocks with these lemmas. For example, `hmn` becomes `muVal_of_pos hq3 hbad`, and `hmu0` becomes `muVal_of_eq_zero hq3 hz`. At line 201 and line 251, `hz` is already `badCountQ … = 0`, so the `omega` side proof is unnecessary.
findings.benefit: The reader gets a documented API for the measure. The nine copies of the unfolding proof, including the four that restate the long RHS, collapse to one-line lemma applications. Future uses can rely on `simp` for the good case instead of hand-built `dite_eq_*` side proofs. Keeping the `pos` equation non-simp avoids unwanted expansion of the proof-dependent `leastGoodAbove` term.
